title: TSMM Agent Interaction Extension Instance v0.13.0
description: Extension schema for modeling trust-relevant aspects of agent-to-agent interaction: service disclosure, capability contracts, session continuity, runtime authorization checkpoints, extension negotiation, opacity constraints, and lateral peer trust.

serviceDescriptor.description: A trust-relevant capability disclosure artifact whose visibility is policy-bound and whose authenticity may be signed. Generalizes Agent Card, OpenID Federation entity statement, and TRQP ecosystem descriptor constructs.

disclosurePolicy.description: Visibility scope of the descriptor. 'public': no authentication required. 'authenticated': extended metadata available after credential presentation. 'restricted': access governed by explicit policy.

endpointSet.description: Published endpoint URIs for this entity.

authenticityBinding.description: Reference to an integrity or signing mechanism confirming authenticity of this descriptor, e.g. a JWK thumbprint or verification method identifier.

skillContract.description: An operational contract for a discrete capability unit, separating what an entity can do (capability) from what it may do under defined modalities, scopes, and policy conditions (operational envelope).

capabilityRef.description: Reference to the capability object this contract governs.

inputModes.description: Accepted input modalities for this capability, e.g. text, structured-data, file-reference.

authorizationScope.description: The authorization boundary under which this skill may be exercised.

policyConditions.description: Policy conditions or constraints that must be satisfied before the skill may be exercised.

examples.description: Illustrative input/output examples for this skill.

peerTrustRelation.description: A trust relationship between lateral agents operating as peers with no pre-existing hierarchical relationship. Distinct from the delegation model, which is hierarchical. Models how trust is established and maintained between peers where neither holds authority over the other.

partyARefs.description: Identifiers of the first lateral party or parties.

partyBRefs.description: Identifiers of the second lateral party or parties.

trustBasis.description: The mechanism through which this peer trust relation was established.

trustScope.description: The bounded scope of what is trusted between these peers.

conditionsForWithdrawal.description: Conditions under which this peer trust relation may be revoked or suspended.

interactionContext.description: A session or conversation scope that groups tasks, messages, and trust decisions into a shared governance context. Extends ExecutionContext to the session level: captures accumulated governance state across a sequence of interactions, including what authority and evidence carry forward and what requires re-authorization.

inheritedAuthorityRefs.description: Authority objects from earlier in the session that remain in force for subsequent turns.

inheritedEvidenceRefs.description: Evidence objects established earlier in the session that carry forward without re-verification.

reAuthorizationPolicy.description: Policy governing when re-authorization is required despite inherited authority, e.g. on scope change, after time threshold, or on resource sensitivity escalation.

terminationReason.description: Reason recorded when this interaction context was closed. Only present after termination.

authorizationCheckpoint.description: A first-class trust event representing a runtime authorization challenge that interrupts or pauses an interaction pending resolution. Distinct from policy evaluation: models the case where evaluation inputs are absent or insufficient and the interaction is suspended until they are provided.

triggerCondition.description: Why this checkpoint was raised. 'policy-gap': policy cannot be evaluated with available attributes. 'auth-required': authentication credential is missing or expired. 'input-required': required input data is absent. 'scope-exceeded': requested action falls outside delegated or contracted scope.

taskRef.description: Optional reference to the specific task or work unit that triggered this checkpoint.

requiredEvidenceRefs.description: Evidence objects that would satisfy this checkpoint if supplied.

resolutionPaths.description: Ordered candidate paths for resolving this checkpoint, e.g. user authentication, principal escalation, evidence retrieval.

opacityBoundary.description: A structural governance constraint declaring what is deliberately unobservable about an agent's operation and the trust and evidence implications of that non-observability. TSMM models what is observable; OpacityBoundary models what is structurally unknowable and how trust decisions must be scoped accordingly.

opaqueComponents.description: Components of the agent's operation that are structurally not observable to counterparties.

evidenceGap.description: Description of what cannot be verified about this agent due to its opacity boundary.

trustScopeConstraint.description: How trust decisions about or involving this agent must be bounded given what cannot be verified.

mitigations.description: Controls that partially compensate for the evidence gap introduced by opacity.

extensionContract.description: A protocol-neutral abstraction for negotiated extension compatibility. Captures extension URI, version, requiredness, negotiated status, and failure handling. Generalizes across A2A, MCP, OpenID Federation, and any extension-carrying protocol. The negotiation record is governance-relevant: silent downgrade without a failure signal creates an audit gap.

requiredness.description: Whether the interaction requires this extension to proceed.

negotiatedStatus.description: Outcome of extension negotiation. 'degraded' signals capability reduction without full rejection.

failureHandling.description: How the system behaves if a required extension cannot be negotiated.

resolutionRecord.description: Optional record of why the negotiation reached its current status.
